questions.q: What is secularism, and why is it important?
answer: Secularism is the principle that the state keeps a distance from religion and treats all religions equally, without having any official state religion.

answer.text: It protects the freedom of every individual to follow, change or reject any religion, so that no one is forced to accept a particular faith.
It protects the members of one religion from being dominated by another, and also protects individuals from being coerced by their own religious community.

In a country as diverse as India, with many religions living side by side, secularism is essential to ensure equality, prevent religious conflict, and allow people of all faiths to live together with dignity and freedom.

questions.q: How does Indian secularism differ from a strict separation of religion and state?
answer: Indian secularism has its own distinctive character.

answer.text: The Indian Constitution makes India a secular state with no official religion. The state does not favour any religion, guarantees freedom of religion as a fundamental right, and treats all faiths equally.

Unlike a strict separation, in which the state never touches religion, the Indian state may intervene in religious matters to ensure equality and reform. For example, it banned untouchability and opened temples to all castes, stepping in when a practice violated fundamental rights.
Thus Indian secularism combines distance and non-interference with the power to intervene for justice, making it both respectful of religion and committed to equality.
